name: Astera Labs
thesis: Connectivity silicon (retimers, Scorpio switches) inside AI racks; Q2 revenue $392M, +104% YoY, Q3 guide $540-560M with Scorpio X set to become the largest product line. Thursday's roughly 2% after-hours dip had no company news behind it and was gone by Friday: $359.93 (+1.0%) at 10:30 ET, a day the whole chip group bid on a soft jobs report. Fubon Buy with a $500 target; consensus $389.95.
risks: Only 8% below the consensus target after the rebound from the Sep 15 low of $251.97, and a tight range under $377.87 is the level the stock has to clear. Few hyperscaler customers, Nvidia NVLink competes directly, and a Seeking Alpha note flags Amazon warrants and mix pressuring margins.

name: Broadcom
thesis: Top custom AI chip (XPU) and AI networking supplier; Q3 FY26 AI revenue $16.7B, +221% YoY, Q4 guide ~$34.8B. Recovered Thursday's 2.2% drop with a 3.7% gain to $356.43 at 10:30 ET as yields fell on the jobs miss, still digesting the up-to-$42B convertible loan to Anthropic. Consensus target $531.85 (+49%), still the widest gap among the AI names.
risks: Broadcom is now supplier, lessor and lender to a customer that lost over $8B operating in 2025 on $4.6B revenue; today's bounce does not change that conflict. China's SASAC is surveying Broadcom switches in state data centres, and the 10-year yield, though off its 5.34% high, is still near 5.2%.
catalyst: Q4 FY2026 earnings ~2026-12-10 (est.); Anthropic IPO pricing; any SASAC guidance on switches

name: SK hynix
thesis: Holds ~58% of HBM revenue share; Q2 operating income KRW 60.5T at a 76% margin, ~9x trailing earnings. Seoul closed Friday at KRW 1,841,000 (+0.4%) in a soft KOSPI; the ADR is $194.81 (+0.7%) at 10:30 ET, 2.5% under its $199.87 52-week high. 15 analysts at Buy, ADR consensus target $252 (+29%).
risks: A Solidigm listing adds an ownership layer; the company says nothing is decided, but the first report knocked the stock about 5%. Micron fell after its own beat, so near-term memory news is priced in; Bernstein cut its target on slower HBM4 pricing and CXMT is closing the gap.
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings ~2026-10-29 (est.); any Solidigm financing decision

name: Bloom Energy
thesis: On-site fuel cells for AI data centres; Q2 revenue $1.07B, +166%, 2026 guide $3.9-4.2B. Up 4.9% to $291.05 at 10:30 ET on the broad bid after the jobs report, no company news found. That is 3% above the $282.82 consensus target, with Barclays at $308 and RBC $335.
risks: Above the consensus target at ~330x earnings, with 5-13% daily swings normal; the Fremont expansion is the bull case, not yet revenue. Oracle's Jupiter force majeure stands (gas pipeline slipped to Feb 2027, fuel-cell air permit due Nov 23). Several class actions pending.
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings 2026-10-27; Jupiter air-quality permit decision by 2026-11-23

name: GE Vernova
thesis: Bottleneck supplier of gas turbines and grid gear for AI power; Q2 orders $24.2B (+88% organic), backlog ~$176B. Eased 0.5% to $982.38 at 10:30 ET, the one large cap on the list lower on a rising tape, after Thursday's 3.9% gain. The BWRX-300 SMR has its first US construction permit and the CEO told a Morgan Stanley conference demand is strong and durable. Consensus target $1,230 (+25%).
risks: Premium multiple on a cyclical business (low target $940, GLJ Sell $470) and the stock gave back some of Thursday's gain. Tariffs cost $100-200M in 2026, offshore wind still loses money, and TVA has no construction date or cost-sharing deal for the SMR.

name: Vertiv Holdings
thesis: Power, thermal and liquid-cooling infrastructure for AI data centres; Q2 net sales $3.27B (+24%, 18% organic) at a 22.6% adjusted operating margin, 2026 guide $14.0B. Up 2.3% to $251.65 at 10:30 ET with the market, a second day higher on no company news. Consensus target $338.22 (+34%); Wells Fargo and BofA are both constructive.
risks: ~57x earnings prices in the guide; Q2 organic growth was 18% with acquisitions and FX doing the rest, so the second half has to accelerate. Hyperscaler capex concentration, and Schneider, Eaton and Asian OEMs compete in liquid cooling. Medium conviction until Q3 confirms the ramp.
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings ~2026-10-22 (est.); KES deal close Q4

name: Robinhood Markets
thesis: Q2 revenue $1.31B (+32%) at a 57% adjusted EBITDA margin. Up 5.0% to $116.65 at 10:30 ET, the best of the Internet names, ending three days of drift on the soft-jobs rally; no company news. Q3 results are set for Oct 27. Consensus target $131 (+12%), Morgan Stanley $150, KeyBanc $140.
risks: Perps and autonomous AI agents draw regulators; two engineers were charged Sep 15 with insider trading on crypto listings. Revenue swings with retail and crypto volumes at ~50x earnings, and the stock is still 24% under its $153.86 high.
catalyst: Robinhood Agents rollout in October; Q3 2026 earnings 2026-10-27

name: MercadoLibre
thesis: LatAm's leading e-commerce and fintech platform; Q2 revenue $10.17B (+50%), the 30th straight quarter above 30%. Up 0.9% to $1,699.60 at 10:30 ET, a small bounce after a 12% slide since Sep 14 on no company news. Consensus target $2,270 (+34%); the one-hour Sao Paulo delivery launch is the new service.
risks: Operating margin is 6.7%, down from 12.2%, as it spends on shipping, credit and one-hour delivery. Nu is competing hard in lending, and a high-yield US backdrop drains emerging-market flows; the 52-week low is $1,495, 12% below the price.

name: Cloudflare
thesis: Edge network that controls bot and AI-agent traffic; Q2 revenue $696M (+36%), 120% net retention. Flat to up 0.2% at $351.75 at 10:30 ET, lagging a strong tape and about 2% under the Sep 22 record, a day after launching Basin (an Iceberg data lake on R2 with no egress fees). The Deutsche Telekom tie-up and a public post-quantum CA (Q1 2027) widen the enterprise story.
risks: Trades 4% above the $337 consensus target at ~47x sales, so any growth miss will be punished. Gross margin fell 320bps to 73.1%; Basin is another product that needs years to show in revenue.

name: Sea Limited
thesis: Q2 revenue $7.8B (+48%): Shopee GMV +28%, Monee loan book +62%, 2026 adjusted EBITDA guide above $1B. Up 0.8% to $96.03 at 10:30 ET, a small bounce after three falling days; still -26% YTD. Average target $157 (+63%) is the widest gap on the list, but nothing is due until Nov 10, so conviction stays medium.
risks: DBS cut to Hold on Sep 30 with the target lowered to $105 from $148, and there is no catalyst for five weeks; $95 is the level to watch, with the 52-week low at $77.05. TikTok Shop and Temu in Southeast Asia, the Brazil push against MELI, Fitch flagging consumer credit risk at SeaBank Indonesia.

name: BYD
thesis: Exports drive growth: September NEV sales 463,561 (+17.0% YoY), overseas 180,700, a fifth straight monthly rise offsetting a weak home market. The shares closed Friday at HK$73.90 (-2.25%), $9.42 at 7.847 HKD per USD, as JPMorgan cut the rating to Neutral from Overweight and the target to HK$88 from HK$124 on weak domestic demand, rising procurement costs and tariffs. Average target HK$125.70 (+70%).
risks: Domestic sales keep shrinking as Geely, Leapmotor (+59% in September) and Xpeng take share; the price war squeezes margins and first-half profit fell 20.5%. The stock is 3.5% above its HK$71.40 52-week low with no buyer on the sales number or the first big-house downgrade, and EU tariffs hang over the export engine. Moved to watch until it holds the low.

name: Keyence Corp
thesis: Machine vision and sensors for factory automation and robotics; fiscal Q1 sales JPY 346.6B (+32.8%), net income +51% to JPY 139.1B, operating margin above 50%. Tokyo closed Friday at JPY 80,270 (-1.15%) after Thursday's JPY 81,200 high, no company news. At 157.53 yen per dollar that is $510. Citi and Goldman Sachs have upgraded; consensus JPY 97,867 (+22%).
risks: The premium multiple (~40x) assumes 30%+ growth. A stronger yen or slower China capex would hit both earnings and the multiple; Toyota's August numbers show Chinese and US auto demand softening. The 52-week high is JPY 87,920, 9% above the price.

name: ASML Holding
thesis: Sole EUV supplier; 2026 guide EUR 43-45B at 54-56% gross margin, 2027 EUV capacity essentially sold out and low-NA EUV capacity set to grow about 30% in 2027. Up 2.9% to $1,860.95 at 10:30 ET with the chip group; no company news. Consensus target $2,095 (+12.6%); bookings on Oct 14 are the next test.
risks: China export limits and proposed US chip tariffs. Sentiment-driven days cut both ways (-7.3% on Sep 14), and the Oct 14 bookings number has to back a rally that has taken the price to within 13% of consensus.

name: Teradyne
thesis: Test equipment for AI and HBM chips (~70% of revenue) plus Universal Robots cobots; Q2 revenue $1.33B, more than double. Up 6.1% to $441.09 at 10:30 ET, the best of the 15 for a third day running, no company news; Friday's move came with the whole chip group. The Magnum E2 memory tester shows at SEMICON West Oct 13-15. Consensus target $446.47, 1% above the price.
risks: Now at the consensus target, so there is no analyst upside left; moved from accumulate to watch rather than chase a third strong day. It was the most volatile name on the list (-13.3% on Sep 14), test orders are lumpy and from a few customers, and the memory trade is priced for good news.

name: Tesla
thesis: Q3 deliveries beat: 486,532 vs the 461,974 company-compiled consensus (+5.3%), production 464,391, so inventory fell by about 22,000. Deliveries are -2.1% YoY but +1.3% on Q2; Model 3/Y were 478,237. Storage missed: 13.7 GWh vs 15.9 GWh expected. The stock is $373.90 (+5.6%) at 10:30 ET, back above $350 and 21% down YTD. Consensus target $396 (+6%). Track it, don't chase it.
risks: Cars are shrinking YoY against BYD and Xiaomi, and the storage miss hits the segment the valuation leans on. 2026 capex tops $25B against $8.5B in 2025 and analysts model about $9.8B of negative free cash flow; Tesla lined up $30B of credit (undrawn). The stock is only 6% from consensus after a jump on a delivery beat.
catalyst: Q3 earnings ~2026-10-21 after close (est.; secondary sources, earlier listed as Oct 28); Roadster demo 2026-10-15
